correctness.rationale: PASS: Units of S(G) are exactly (empty,g) and idempotents exactly (A,1), with Boolean union atoms singletons. Thus a semigroup isomorphism gives group isomorphism phi and atom permutation s satisfying s(ga)=phi(g)s(a), whence s(a)=phi(a)t and F(A,g)=(phi(A)t,phi(g)). For the pointed inverse semigroup, minimum idempotent ({1},1), atoms e_g=({1,g},1), and unique nonidempotent with range e_g equal a_g=({1,g},g) recover the multiplication: a_g a_h has range support {1,g,gh}, and its second coordinate distinguishes gh=1. Thus phi is multiplicative. Factorization (A,g)=(A,1)a_g completes all-group reconstruction, including the trivial group. Composition conjugations yield Hol(G), |G| distinct pointed copies, faithful inner unit conjugations. Explicitly inspected standalone checker for C1/C2/C3/C4/V4/S3; finite cases are corroboration, proof uses arbitrary finite G.
